findings.headline: Migrate this two-argument createEffect call.
findings.why: Solid 1 reads the second argument as the initial value, but Solid 2's signature is createEffect(compute, effectFn, options), so the second argument is the apply callback that receives each computed value. A second argument that is syntactically an arrow or function expression is the Solid 2 apply callback and is not reported; this call's second argument is not.
findings.guidance: If the second argument is a Solid 1 initial value, move it to a default parameter of the compute callback and pass the side effect as the second argument: createEffect((prev = INITIAL_VALUE) => compute(prev), (value) => { ... }). If the second argument is already the apply callback, the call is split and needs no change. Stop and ask when you cannot tell which of the two it is.

findings.headline: Migrate this 3-argument createEffect call.
findings.why: Solid 1's signature is createEffect(fn, initialValue, options), but Solid 2's is createEffect(compute, effectFn, options): the second argument is the apply callback and options stay third. A second argument that is syntactically an arrow or function expression is the Solid 2 apply callback and is not reported; this call's second argument is not.
findings.guidance: Move the initial value to a default parameter of the compute callback, pass the side effect as the second argument, and keep the options object third, dropping any option Solid 2 does not support: createEffect((prev = INITIAL_VALUE) => compute(prev), (value) => { ... }, options). If the second argument is already the apply callback, only the options need checking. Stop and ask when you cannot tell the role of each argument.
